meta.description: Daily tracking state for F-1/SEVP/DS-2019 policy monitoring, focused on relevance to a Virginia Tech student who may need an extra semester to finish their degree.

items.title: DHS Final Rule: Fixed Time Period of Admission & Extension of Stay (ends Duration of Status) for F, J, I nonimmigrants
items.summary: DHS published a final rule (doc. 2026-14439) on Jul 17, 2026, ending open-ended Duration of Status for F-1 students, effective Sep 15, 2026. Students get a fixed 'Admit Until Date' capped at 4 years (24 months for language programs); anyone needing more time must file Form I-539 (Extension of Stay) with USCIS in addition to the existing DSO SEVIS extension -- the I-539 EOS filing fee is reported as $420 filed online / $470 by paper. A timely-filed EOS gives up to 240 days of authorized stay while pending. The rule also shortens the F-1 post-completion grace period from 60 to 30 days for anyone who travels/re-enters or gets an EOS approval after the effective date. Students already in D/S status who remain continuously in the U.S. without leaving/re-entering keep transition protections, but only up to a hard outside cap of Nov 14, 2030 (4 years + 60-day grace period measured from the Sep 15, 2026 effective date). DHS has discretion to postpone, until as late as Sep 14, 2028, implementation of the specific provisions restricting mid-program school transfers, changes in educational objective (major/level), and progression to same- or lower-level programs, if DHS determines full implementation isn't feasible by the Sep 15, 2026 effective date -- this discretionary postponement option applies only to those specific transfer/education-level provisions, not to the core fixed-admission-period change itself. New today: USCIS will publish revised editions of Form I-539 and Form I-765 effective Sep 15, 2026, aligned to the new fixed-admission-period process -- the current 08/28/24 edition of Form I-539 will still be accepted if postmarked or e-filed before Sep 15, 2026, but rejected on/after that date, after which only the new 09/15/26 edition is accepted. Also new today: NAFSA and the Presidents' Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration have moved into formal preparation for a legal challenge to the rule (per a dedicated nafsa.org/legal-defense-DS page, last updated Jul 30, 2026) -- litigation is being prepared, focused on documenting concrete, immediate, irreparable harms institutions can show, but no lawsuit had actually been filed as of this run.
items.notes: No lawsuit had been filed and no Congressional Review Act disapproval resolution had passed as of this run (checked 2026-08-17, fourth check). Targeted congress.gov searches today for a CRA disapproval resolution specific to this rule again found nothing beyond generic CRA background and unrelated joint resolutions -- congress.gov itself was directly reachable today (a change from prior runs), it simply doesn't have a matching resolution. NAFSA remains publicly opposed and, new today, its legal-defense-DS page confirms NAFSA and the Presidents' Alliance are formally preparing (not yet filing) a legal challenge. SEVP stakeholder webinar remains scheduled for Mon, Aug 31, 2026, 2-3pm ET per Study in the States, confirmed today via a secondary source that no advance registration is required. Separately continuing to track the 30-Senator letter on visa interview delays as its own item below since it concerns visa *issuance*, not the admission-period change itself.

items.title: DHS regulatory review of OPT / STEM OPT (RIN 1653-AA97) — no NPRM published yet
items.summary: DHS confirmed in a Jan 9, 2026 letter it is re-evaluating the scope and duration of OPT and STEM OPT, with a rulemaking entry (RIN 1653-AA97, titled 'Practical Training') in the Unified Regulatory Agenda covering worker protection, fraud prevention, national security, and SEVP oversight goals. As of this run, no Notice of Proposed Rulemaking has been published in the Federal Register. A single secondary source (americanbazaaronline.com, Aug 11, 2026) reports the government's own unified agenda lists an NPRM target of February 2027 for this rule. OPT and STEM OPT remain fully operational and unchanged today. Upgraded to Confirmed today: a direct site:reginfo.gov search reached the official reginfo.gov entry for RIN 1653-AA97 itself, which describes the proposed rule's purpose in DHS's own words -- to 'better align practical training to the goals and objectives of the program' and 'address fraud and national security concerns, protect U.S. workers from being displaced by foreign nationals, and enhance [SEVP's] capacity to oversee the program.' This confirms the rulemaking docket's existence and current (pre-NPRM) stage directly from an official U.S. government source, though it does not confirm any NPRM has been published -- that step still has not happened. Relevant because many students planning an extra semester are also relying on post-completion OPT/STEM OPT timing.
items.notes: No OPT/STEM OPT NPRM has been published as of 2026-08-17 (fourth check today). Confirmation status upgraded today (see summary) after reginfo.gov itself was successfully reached via WebSearch for the first time in this tracker's run history -- it had been listed as an unavailable source category for 5+ consecutive prior runs. Will keep watching for actual NPRM publication in the Federal Register.

items.title: ICE/HSI announces nationwide OPT fraud crackdown: 10,000+ students linked to 'suspect employers'
items.source: Press reporting of ICE/HSI press conference (Acting Director Todd Lyons)
items.summary: At a May 12, 2026 press conference, Acting ICE Director Todd Lyons and Acting HSI Associate Director John Condon announced that federal investigators had identified more than 10,000 F-1/STEM OPT students linked to 'highly suspect employers' -- among the top 25 OPT-employing companies reviewed. HSI site visits across eight states (TX, VA, GA, IL, NY, NJ, NC, FL) reportedly found empty buildings, locked doors, residential addresses listed as worksites, shell companies, and offshore payroll/HR arrangements; in one Northern Texas case an employer claimed 500 OPT students but had only 3 actual employees on site. Lyons called it 'only the tip of the iceberg.' Directly relevant to any student counting on post-completion OPT/STEM OPT -- especially under an extended timeline -- since it signals intensified employer-level scrutiny and potential SEVIS/EAD complications for students whose employer gets flagged, even if the student did nothing wrong.
items.notes: Still widely reported by many independent outlets describing the same May 12, 2026 press conference (today added thepienews.com's interview-style piece quoting the ICE director calling OPT a 'magnet for fraud', reinforcing but not newly confirming the claim). Targeted site:ice.gov and site:dhs.gov searches today again did not surface an official press release, transcript, or statement on ice.gov/newsroom or dhs.gov matching this specific announcement -- both domains were reachable today and returned other relevant, current SEVP/CPT material, so this is a genuine gap in official coverage of this specific claim rather than a source-access problem. Will keep searching official sources for a matching statement or follow-on enforcement actions (indictments, SEVIS terminations tied to this probe).

items.title: USCIS Policy Alert PA-2026-05: officers may deny incomplete filings without issuing an RFE/NOID first
items.summary: Effective Aug 5, 2026, USCIS updated Policy Manual guidance so adjudicators may, at their discretion, deny a benefit request lacking required initial evidence or failing to establish eligibility without first issuing an RFE or NOID, and may set RFE response deadlines shorter than the prior 12-week norm (the 14-day international-mail grace period was also eliminated). Directly relevant to F-1 students filing Form I-539 (Extension of Stay) or I-765 under the new fixed-admission-period regime: an incomplete EOS package can now be denied outright with no chance to cure.
items.notes: No changes found today (fourth check). Confirmed via the official USCIS newsroom alert and the underlying Policy Alert PA-2026-05 PDF, which updates USCIS-PM E.6, E.9, and E.10, effective for requests pending or filed on/after Aug 5, 2026.

items.title: SEVP Broadcast Message BCM 2608-01: DSOs warned on CPT authorization liability, increased scrutiny
items.summary: On Aug 12, 2026, SEVP issued Broadcast Message 2608-01, 'Reminder of Liability for DSOs Regarding CPT Authorization,' to every PDSO/DSO at SEVP-certified schools. SEVP says it has observed a rise in Curricular Practical Training (CPT) authorizations that do not meet regulatory requirements -- specifically CPT not constituting an integral part of an established curriculum -- and is increasing scrutiny of CPT approvals. The message does not change the CPT regulation itself and DHS's July D/S final rule separately stated it 'does not prohibit or eliminate Day-1 CPT' and 'does not make substantive changes to CPT.' But it signals stepped-up enforcement: schools found authorizing CPT improperly risk investigation and loss of SEVP certification. Washington State University's Aug 7, 2026 international-office advisory (published before SEVP's Aug 12 message, so an independent, earlier move) announced ISSS there will stop approving full-time CPT during the academic year starting Spring 2027, except for programs with an explicit mandatory-internship curriculum requirement -- an early example of a university preemptively tightening its own CPT approval practices. No indication yet that Virginia Tech's Cranwell International Center has announced a similar change; VT's CPT page still describes standard part-time/full-time CPT eligibility rules with no dated policy update.
items.notes: No regulatory text has changed -- this remains a compliance/enforcement reminder, not a rulemaking. No new VT-specific update found today; Virginia Tech's international.vt.edu/employment/cpt.html was reached directly again today and still shows standard, unchanged CPT guidance. Additional secondary legal-blog coverage found today (szetolaw.com) describing the same Aug 12 broadcast message, no new facts.

items.title: 30 Senators press State Dept (Rubio) to clear F/M/J student visa interview backlog before fall term
items.source: Office of Sen. Alex Padilla (official press release) / press reporting
items.summary: On Aug 11, 2026, 30 U.S. Senators led by Sen. Alex Padilla sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio saying 'no timely visa appointments are available for students at some embassies and consulates' during peak season, and asking the State Department to restore priority to F, M, and J visa interviews, extend interview waivers for vetted returning students, and boost consular staffing before fall term starts. The letter gives State 30 days to respond to 10 questions -- a deadline around Sep 10, 2026, after most fall terms have already begun. Not a rule change, but directly relevant to any F-1 student (including someone on an extended timeline) who needs to obtain a new visa stamp or renew one to travel and re-enter, especially once the Sep 15, 2026 D/S-to-fixed-admission-period transition takes effect.
items.notes: No State Department response found yet (not due until ~Sep 10, 2026, third check today). travel.state.gov was reached directly today via WebSearch for the first time in this tracker's run history (it had shown 8 consecutive quiet runs) -- its Visa Appointment Wait Times page confirms wait-time data is updated monthly with the most recent update dated Jul 21, 2026, but contains no reference to this letter or a State Department reply. Will keep tracking for a State Department response or a change in interview-scheduling practice.

items.title: Reported $100,000 fee under consideration for OPT / post-completion work authorization
items.source: Press reporting (Forbes, Bloomberg, ICEF Monitor, The PIE News, Higher Ed Dive)
items.summary: Multiple outlets report the administration is weighing a $100,000 fee applicable to OPT employment authorization (and by extension STEM OPT), modeled on the now-struck-down $100,000 H-1B fee proclamation. As of this run, no signed proclamation or DHS proposed rule/fee schedule has been reported for an OPT fee -- unlike the H-1B fee, which was signed via proclamation on Sep 19, 2025 and then struck down by a federal judge on Jun 8, 2026. Immigration attorneys quoted say an OPT fee is unlikely to survive legal challenge absent Congressional authorization, citing that H-1B precedent plus a Jul 24, 2026 appellate rejection of the administration's appeal. Who would pay (student/university/employer) remains unresolved. Directly relevant to students weighing an extra semester who are also counting on post-completion OPT/STEM OPT to work in the U.S. afterward.
items.notes: Still no DHS/USCIS/.gov statement, proposed rule, or signed proclamation found confirming or denying this as of 2026-08-17 (fourth check today). No proclamation has been signed. Reporting continues to cite the First Circuit's rejection of the administration's appeal in the related H-1B $100,000 fee litigation as the key legal headwind to an OPT-fee proclamation surviving challenge.

items.title: NAFSA/JB International report: fall 2026 international enrollment projected to fall ~9.5% (~111,000 students) amid visa crackdown
items.source: NAFSA: Association of International Educators / JB International (research report, press reporting)
items.summary: A report released Aug 11, 2026 by NAFSA and research firm JB International, based on institutional responses to IIE's Spring 2026 Snapshot survey, projects fall 2026 international enrollment at U.S. colleges will fall about 9.5% (~111,000 fewer students), citing declining applications, visa-appointment bottlenecks, and newly restrictive immigration policy (including the D/S final rule) as converging headwinds. Estimated economic impact: ~$3.4 billion in lost local spending and ~39,000-40,000 jobs. This is a research/economic-impact projection rather than a new rule -- it is being tracked here as evidence of how seriously the sector expects the policy changes above to bite, which is relevant context (not itself an actionable status change) for a student weighing an extra semester.
items.notes: This is a private-association economic/enrollment projection, not a government policy claim, so there is no .gov document that would ever 'confirm' it in the same sense as the other items -- it is tracked as 'Reported, unconfirmed' per the tracker's default schema, but readers should treat that label as 'not a government-verifiable fact' rather than 'possibly false.' No change in the core finding today (fourth check), but found reinforcing independent coverage: a U.S. News piece (Aug 5, 2026) on enrollment anxiety/fear, and a Fitch Ratings analysis (via Higher Ed Dive) warning the new visa limits could hurt international enrollment and university revenue -- both echo the same trend from separate analytical angles.
